extraction_method: manual structured extraction from Wise 2023 Remittances Report (20 pages) — macro market data and first-person sender testimonials

sending_country_scope.quote: This report will focus on 12 countries, all in the G20, which are considered 'remittance sending countries'

value.Australia: half of the population has at least one parent born overseas
value.Canada: record number of new migrants in 2022; trend over last decade of increased immigration
value.Japan: close to 2 million migrant workers; newer routes from Vietnam, Philippines, China overtaking traditional ones

recipient_use_of_funds.value: Over 75% of recipients use remittances for essentials — food, medicine, keeping children in school, roof over their head
recipient_use_of_funds.quote: Unicef estimates that [over 75% of] remittances are used for the essentials – to keep children in school, to feed families, to keep a roof over their head

global_remittance_volume_2022_usd_bn.quote: remittances volumes globally reached just under $800 billion

g20_sending_volume_2021_usd_bn.quote: In 2021, G20 sending countries sent just under $200 billion in remittances

un_sdg_cost_target_2030.quote: UN Sustainable Development Goals... formalising their commitment to lowering the cost of remittances to 3% or lower by 2030

fx_margin_share_of_fees.value: approximately 50% of global cross-border payment fees are in the form of FX margin
fx_margin_share_of_fees.quote: A McKinsey report found that half of global cross-border payment fees are in the form of FX margin

hidden_fee_annual_impact_eu.value: €4.6 billion ($5 billion) per year lost by European remitters in fees
hidden_fee_annual_impact_eu.quote: European remitters lost €4.6 billion ($5 billion) in fees

informal_channel_usage.value: South Africa: large proportion of remittance flows are through informal channels due to regulatory friction (tiered licensing caps per-transaction limits)
informal_channel_usage.quote: a large proportion flows through informal channels... currency controls have stifled competition

fee_awareness_gap.value: Only 20% of Canadian consumers could correctly identify exchange rate markups as part of the cost
fee_awareness_gap.quote: only 20% of consumers could correctly identify exchange rate markups as part of that cost. This means consumers lose money unwittingly

inflation_eroded_purchasing_power.value: 2023: 0.75% reduction in value of remittance flows vs 2021 (inflation-adjusted); Japan weak yen further eroded sender purchasing power

dependence_lifeline_for_recipients.value: Remittances often spike in times of conflict, natural disaster, or financial hardship in the receiving country. Remittance volumes exceed ODA in countries like Australia, Italy, United States
dependence_lifeline_for_recipients.quote: Remittances often spike in times of conflict, natural disaster or financial hardship in the receiving country

hidden_fee_practice_as_consumer_harm.value: 'Junk fees' framing — Wise argues hidden exchange-rate markups are the primary mechanism of consumer harm. Not fraud in the criminal sense, but an exploitation pattern.

fatf_grey_list_impact.value: South Africa's recent FATF Grey List addition made attracting competition more challenging, keeping prices high — indirectly increasing vulnerability to informal-channel fraud

transparency_as_trust_signal.value: Wise's thesis: transparent pricing (real-time benchmark FX rate, no markup) is the solution to the trust deficit in remittances. Consumers should be able to 'pick a money transfer service with their eyes wide open.'
transparency_as_trust_signal.quote: Consumers should be able to pick a money transfer service with their eyes wide open

bank_to_fintech_switching.value: First-person Hungarian sender: started with banks, switched when costs were high. Suggests bank-to-fintech migration among first-time remitters.
bank_to_fintech_switching.quote: In the beginning we did it through banks, and surprisingly the costs of the remittances were so high…

value.use_case: supporting wife's father (Malaysia) and mother (Indonesia); early-retired couple
value.pain_point: hidden foreign-exchange fees eating into transfers; also domestic surprise fees

value.use_case: sponsoring youths from medical missions (17+ years); many destitute after pandemic with overdue bills

suitable_for_grounding_fields: transfer_service_loyalty (Wise specifically; broader fintech migration from banks)
loss_tolerance_usd (via inflation-eroded purchasing power and fee awareness gap)
remittance_cadence (from first-person stories: regular monthly support patterns)
not_suitable_for_grounding_fields: specific fraud events (advocacy report, not a fraud typology)
persona_grounding_implications.behavioral_evidence_grade_when_used: C — industry behavioral research (Wise advocacy report). First-person testimonials are narrative but curated for the report's policy arguments, not random-sampled.
persona_grounding_implications.caveat: Wise is an advocacy publication — the framing (hidden fees = primary harm) reflects Wise's market position. Use the macro statistics with confidence; treat the policy arguments as one industry viewpoint, not neutral regulatory truth.
